headline.meaning: The dominant tension this quarter is between rapidly expanding multi-agent/tool-use capability and the comparatively thinner scalable-oversight work meant to supervise those systems.
headline.capability_focus: Multi-agent LLM scaling across task structures, agentic software-engineering context management, and LLM-based topic modeling — systems that coordinate, use tools, and act over long interaction loops.
headline.safety_focus: Scalable oversight applied to agentic settings, including data-sovereignty-aware tutoring deployment and analysis of when multi-agent scaling actually helps or fails.
headline.why_it_matters: Multi-agent/tool-use capability grew ~203% per quarter versus ~87% for scalable oversight (gap 1.16, capability-to-safety volume ratio only 0.32), and this is the single pairing flagged as safety-lagging, meaning supervision methods are not keeping pace with the autonomy being deployed.

tabs.divergence: Most pairings actually show safety growing faster than capability — deceptive alignment (+513% vs +274% RSI), CoT faithfulness (+269% vs +50% reasoning), agentic monitoring (+771% vs +266% autonomy), and evals (+725% vs -12.5% frontier scaling). The one clear laggard is scalable oversight against multi-agent/tool-use, where capability outruns oversight and volume is thin. The picture is a safety community sprinting to catch up on autonomy and self-improvement risks while oversight of tool-using multi-agent systems remains under-resourced.
tabs.velocity: The steepest momentum is in Self-Improvement Risk & Control (+1589%), Agentic Behavior Monitoring (+771%), Evals & Dangerous-Capability Benchmarks (+725%), and Deceptive Alignment (+513%), signaling a decisive pivot toward monitoring and evaluating autonomous, self-improving systems. Frontier/Scaling capability is the only contracting topic (-12.5%), suggesting attention is shifting from raw scaling toward agentic deployment and its governance. Reward Hacking safety accelerated (+143%) off a very small base (8.5/qtr), so its momentum is real but still low-volume.
tabs.sentiment: Rising critical share concentrates in Reward Hacking (34.9%, +27.2pts), Frontier/Scaling (42%, +15.7pts), Deceptive Alignment (36.7%, +15.3pts), and Evals (41.2%, +14.8pts), indicating growing skepticism about robustness and honest evaluation as these systems deploy. In contrast, agentic capability and monitoring carry low critical shares (10.7% and 12.5%), which suggests fast-growing agent work is still framed optimistically rather than critically. That combination — high volume, low criticality in agentic autonomy — is itself a warning sign.
tabs.quadrant: Nearly every safety and capability topic sits in the 'hot' quadrant, reflecting broad, simultaneous acceleration across the safety-relevant landscape this quarter. Only RL/RLHF and Frontier/Scaling capability register as 'established', consistent with maturing, slower-growing areas. There is little visible white space, meaning the field is crowding into agentic autonomy, self-improvement, and evaluation rather than opening genuinely new fronts.
tabs.citations: No rapid-growth or sleeper citation movers were reported this quarter, so citation-based signals are currently uninformative. This likely reflects the recency of the surge topics — agentic monitoring, deceptive alignment, and evals are growing too fast to have accumulated citation histories yet. Judgments here should rely on submission velocity and sentiment rather than citation dynamics.
